name: discord
description: Discord community reads — the official MCP only searches developer docs, so message history needs a bot-token community server

requirements: Discord application with a bot token
Bot invited to the servers it may read
Message Content privileged intent enabled — otherwise the Gateway closes with code 4014
VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY permissions on the target channels
notes: Discord has NO official MCP server that reads or sends messages in your servers or DMs. The official MCP (https://docs.discord.com/mcp) only searches developer documentation (3 read-only doc tools).
Message reads need a community server driven by a DISCORD bot token — the leading maintained one is barryyip0625/mcp-discord (MIT).
The npm `mcp-discord` build is stale (v1.3.4, 22 tools); the GitHub build is v1.5.1 (46 tools), stdio by default with optional HTTP. Register the GitHub build, not the npm one.
Reading history needs VIEW_CHANNEL + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY; the Message Content intent is required to read message text.
Discord's native Search Guild Messages endpoint (2026-03-19) needs READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY + MESSAGE_CONTENT; error 110000 means the guild is not yet indexed.
Self-bot servers (account-token logins) violate Discord's terms of service and are not an option.
Community servers can write (messages, channels, roles, moderation). Dry-run: @discord-mcp/core exposes MCP_WRITE_MODE=preview (blocks all mutations) and MCP_DRY_RUN, plus per-guild allow-lists.
The npm mcp-discord build lags the GitHub release — npm is 1.3.4 (22 tools), the repo ships 1.5.1 (46 tools). Prefer a pinned GitHub spec.
Several public MCP catalogs list `npx @discord/mcp-server` — that package does not exist on npm (404). Treat those catalogs as unreliable.

upstreamTools: official docs MCP — 3 read-only documentation search tools
community: send message, channel/role management, moderation, webhooks
